title: Add representative workload suite to nightly canary + gating mode for release branches
author: Connor O'Brien
body: Context: As part of the Q1 2026 “Perf baseline & representative workload suite” project, we need the representative suite to run continuously (nightly) and also to be usable as a release gate for runtime release branches. This PR wires the representative suite runner into perf-canary with two execution modes: (1) nightly mode (signal + trend) and (2) gating mode (pass/fail) intended for release/* branches. Summary of changes: - Adds a new job definition for the representative suite (chat streaming, long-context prefill, embeddings high-QPS; tool-calling is stubbed in config but not enabled by default yet). - Introduces a `mode` flag: `nightly` vs `gating`. Nightly publishes full metric payloads and trends; gating evaluates a smaller set of canonical metrics against threshold config and emits a single PASS/FAIL with links to artifacts. - Adds threshold configuration files keyed by (model_family, workload, gpu_sku, region) with explicit metric boundaries: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95, throughput (tokens/s or req/s for embeddings), plus guardrail saturation signals. - Adds result reporting integration: JSON summary + a markdown report posted to the run output (and to the existing perf-canary comment bot when invoked from a PR workflow). - Adds a “compare-to-baseline” helper that reads the baseline anchor from the run manifest (per ADR-0172) and computes deltas with a simple noise model (min sample size + absolute and relative thresholds). - Adds routing behavior: nightly runs post to #perf-canary (non-paging); gating runs post to #perf-triage (non-paging) and only page on repeated failures (3 consecutive gating failures on the same release branch + same cohort). Important operational notes: - Gating is intentionally fail-closed for release branches (i.e., it will block promotion) but has an explicit override mechanism via a signed config exception (see `docs/gating-exceptions.md`). - We treat missing baseline for a cohort as “SKIP” (non-blocking) to avoid halting releases when a new cohort is added before the baseline sweep catches up. - Cold vs warm cache: gating evaluates both when available; nightly always reports both. By default, gating fails only on cold regressions (warm regressions are warnings) until we finish calibrating cache variance across SKUs. Related: - Linear: ENG-4828 - Confluence: Perf regression policy & thresholds (company standard) - ADR-0172 run manifest schema (consumed by this runner) Testing: - Added unit tests for threshold parsing + delta evaluation. - Ran a dry-run on us-east/H100 with a known-good baseline anchor; verified PASS in gating mode and successful artifact upload. - Simulated a regression by pinning an older baseline + forcing a degraded threshold; verified FAIL output and Slack routing. Rollout plan: - Enable nightly representative suite runs first (starting next scheduled window) and observe variance panels for 1 week. - Enable gating mode for `release/runtime-*` branches after Sana/Sean confirm calibrated thresholds for H100 + A100 cohorts. - Expand to eu-west once baseline sweep completes for that region. Notes / TODO: - Tool/function-calling workload is present in config but not scheduled; will land separately once the generator stabilizes. - Some cohorts are commented out pending L40S baseline completion.
commits: perf-canary: add representative suite job scaffolding and runner entrypoint
perf-canary: implement nightly vs gating mode switch + CLI flags
thresholds: add initial q1-2026 representative suite threshold config (us-east H100/A100)
reporting: add markdown summary + artifact links (manifest, metrics, traces pointer)
eval: add delta computation + minimum sample size enforcement
docs: add gating exceptions policy and dry-run instructions
tests: add parsing + evaluation unit tests for thresholds
conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Nightly vs gating separation looks good. Two concerns: (1) paging behavior and (2) what happens when baseline data is missing. We should not page on the first week of rollout, and missing baseline should not block release. Also, can we add a link to the run manifest in the summary so oncall can drill into env capture quickly?

Connor O'Brien (author): Agreed. Updated Slack routing so nothing pages by default; only repeated failures page (3 consecutive) and only for release branches. Missing baseline now yields SKIP (non-blocking) with an explicit log line and report section. Added manifest link to both JSON and markdown report.

Sana Farid (review): Please tighten the evaluator: right now it’s purely relative delta. For TTFT at low values, relative-only can be noisy. Can we do relative OR absolute thresholds (i.e., pass if delta < max(abs_ms, rel_pct))? Also enforce a minimum N for p99.

Connor O'Brien (author): Implemented `max(abs, rel)` rule per metric. Added `min_samples` per cohort and a hard floor for p99 evaluation. Unit tests added; see `internal/thresholds/evaluator_test.go`.

Rina Kobayashi (review): Config format is close to what benchmark-lab emits, but the workload naming needs to match the suite keys (chat_streaming vs chat-streaming). Otherwise we’ll end up with silent SKIPs. Also, please ensure the report includes the workload seed so we can re-run the same shape.

Connor O'Brien (author): Normalized workload keys to snake_case across suite + thresholds. Added validation to fail the job if a threshold file references an unknown workload key. Report now includes `workload_seed` from the manifest and prints the suite revision string.

Allison Grant (review): Please align metric names/tags with the metrics dictionary draft: TTFT/TPOT should be explicitly “server-side” and exclude client read time. Can you add a note to the docs and ensure the report uses those names verbatim?

Connor O'Brien (author): Updated report labels to `ttft_server_ms` and `tpot_server_ms` and added a short measurement boundary note in `docs/representative-suite-ops.md` referencing the shared definitions.
Sofia Ivanova (review): For gating mode, can we include queue wait and batch assembly time as secondary signals? Not for pass/fail yet, but printed as context to speed triage.
Connor O'Brien (author): Added a “diagnostics” section to the markdown summary that prints queue_wait_p95_ms and batch_assembly_p95_ms when present in the metrics payload (non-blocking).
Sean Gallagher (approval): Looks good with the routing tweaks + SKIP behavior. Approved after latest CI is green.
Sana Farid (approval): Threshold evaluator logic now matches the policy doc expectations. Approving.
